title: TE Jack Eubanks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Items 2 and 3 were sustained; Items 1, 4, and 5 were not sustained. No express relief was stated.
first_summary: Complainants challenged a called Presbytery meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adjudication sustained objections to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote and ordering the dissolved commission to reconvene and reconsider an earlier action. It rejected challenges to the called meeting, Presbytery's involvement with membership, and its receipt of another complaint.
summary: Complainants challenged a called Presbytery meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adjudication sustained objections to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote and ordering the dissolved commission to reconvene and revote. A commission with power could be dismissed only by a two-thirds vote under Robert’s Rules; no separate ground was stated for the reconvening issue. Challenges to the meeting, Presbytery’s membership action, and its receipt of another complaint were not sustained. No relief was specified.
